habitat: Pairs and family groups in forest, well-developed riverine forest and exotic plantations. By day it roosts in large trees close to the trunk.
summary: A fairly common, localised resident. It has a yellow bill, no ear tufts, large pale eye orbits around dark eyes, and barred underparts. The immature is darker, with smaller eye orbits. The male calls a rapid HU-hu, HU-hu-hu, hu-hu, and the female answers with a higher whoo. The Kemp name Wood Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: No ear tufts. Dark brown above, including the surround of the facial disc. Large pale spectacle-like eye orbits surround dark eyes.

underparts.pattern: Finely barred brown on whitish underparts.

head.pattern: The immature has smaller eye orbits and darker colouring.

viewNotes.note: Large pale eye orbits around dark eyes, and no ear tufts. The bill is yellow.
Dark brown above and finely barred brown on whitish underparts.
The underside in flight is not described.
The immature has smaller eye orbits and darker colouring.

calls.description: The male calls a rapid 'HU-hu, HU-hu-hu, hu-hu' and the female replies with a higher 'whoo'. The grade A call is from Zambia. The filename also names a fiery-necked nightjar, so another bird may be present. No Kruger recording was found. The filename is XC581119-African Wood Owl (call) 20200703,NyachisalaForest,Kakoma,Northwestern,ZAMBIA_[+fieryneckednightjar].mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common, localised resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The eyes are only described as dark. The grade A call is from Zambia and its filename names a nightjar. The photograph is dark. The Kemp name Wood Owl and the code RB were left unchanged.
